title: BusinessIntelligenceUpdate
description: Slack Message 1 and its web counterpart (HAR-129 section 5): what changed in the account because Event N arrived, and why it matters. Every change claim carries its own evidence; there is deliberately no confidence field, because a score is not a trace. Slack and web render this object and the AccountChange it points at.

claims.description: What changed, one claim per material change, taken from the state diff.

graph_diff_items.description: The elements of the event's graph diff (GET /events/{id}/graph-diff) this claim also rests on: attributed to the event, of a kind that carries the claim's dimension, and evidence-linked to one of the claim's activities. Absent when none qualifies; the claim is still cited through evidence_refs.

knowledge_refs.description: Previous company knowledge that applies (ids of knowledge objects whose applicability check passed); empty when none does.

account_map_ref.description: What 'View account map' opens: the account graph at this state, with the graph diff highlighted.

transition.description: Required, nullable. The relationship-state transition of the account (ADR-0012), restated from its StateTransition: the one this event touched (touched_by_event true), or, when the event touched none, the account's open transition labelled unchanged (touched_by_event false); null when the account has neither (status 'none'). CANDIDATE and UNRESOLVED name the facts still missing; CONFIRMED has none required. Written by the deterministic detector, never by a model.

touched_by_event.description: true: this event moved the transition. false: the event did not touch it; it is the account's open transition, shown as unchanged.

model.description: The model that wrote the prose; null when the update was built from templates over the cited facts (the Play writer, HAR-124).
